screening.reason: Inclusion 2,3: resting-state fMRI diagnostic classification (ASD vs TD) on ABIDE-I single-site (NYU, UM) and multi-site subsets using a hybrid 3D CNN / 3D Convolutional LSTM model.

evidence_spans.text: Our results show that the proposed model achieves state of the art results on single sites with F1-scores of 0.78 and 0.7 on NYU and UM sites, respectively.
evidence_spans.claim: Main predictive result: F1 0.78 (NYU) and 0.7 (UM) for single-site classification.

evidence_spans.text: We preprocessed the data with the Conﬁgurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes (C-PAC) and the fMRI volumes are downsampled to 4 mm in MNI.
evidence_spans.claim: Preprocessing pipeline is C-PAC with 4mm MNI downsampling; no ROI atlas used (raw 4D volumes).

evidence_spans.text: For single sites experiments, we use the NYU and UM sites from ABIDE-I. Those provide the highest number of balanced (ASD/typically developing (TD)) subjects with 184 and 110 subjects respectively.
evidence_spans.claim: Single-site cohorts: NYU 184 subjects, UM 110 subjects.

evidence_spans.text: For the multi-site experiment we used ABIDE-I with 19 sites and 1100 subjects.
We report 5-fold cross validation mean F1-score and accuracy for the experiments in Table 1.
evidence_spans.claim: Evaluation uses 5-fold cross-validation (no leave-site-out scheme described).

evidence_spans.text: The results show that the proposed architecture 3DCNN C-LSTM outperforms other models on single site experiments by achieving mean test accuracies and F1 scores of 0.77 and 0.78 respectively for the NYU site and 0.71 and 0.7 on the UM site.

3DCNN C-LSTM however also shows a degraded performance in multi-site
environment as evidenced by the results on ABIDE-1 data that features 19 sites.
evidence_spans.claim: Performance degrades on the multi-site ABIDE-I evaluation relative to single-site.

evidence_spans.text:
We attribute the loss of performance of our model to the heterogeneity of the
data acquired from diﬀerent scanners with diﬀerent scanning parameters.
evidence_spans.claim: Authors attribute multi-site performance loss to scanner/acquisition heterogeneity.

assessments.support: N per site is reported (NYU 184, UM 110, multi-site 1100 across 19 sites) but no explicit QC/motion exclusion rule is stated for arriving at these counts.

"We preprocessed the data with the Conﬁgurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes (C-PAC) and the fMRI volumes are downsampled to 4 mm in MNI." — full pipeline specified; no atlas needed since raw 4D volumes are used.
ASD/TD labels are taken from the ABIDE-I phenotype files; the specific diagnostic instrument/criteria are not described in this paper.

Multi-site evaluation uses pooled 5-fold cross-validation with no leave-site-out scheme or site covariate/harmonisation, despite the authors themselves attributing degraded multi-site performance to site/scanner heterogeneity.

risk_of_bias.summary: Pipeline and per-site Ns are clearly reported, but no motion/QC rule is given, diagnostic label source is not elaborated, and the multi-site model is evaluated with pooled cross-validation rather than a leave-site-out design, despite acknowledged site heterogeneity effects.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction study; ABIDE-I single-site cohorts (NYU 184, UM 110 subjects) and a multi-site cohort (19 sites, 1100 subjects)
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed raw 4D resting-state fMRI volumes (4mm MNI) classified end-to-end with a hybrid 3D CNN + bidirectional 3D convolutional LSTM, evaluated with 5-fold cross-validation and compared against several published deep-learning ABIDE classifiers
narrative_row.outcomes: 3DCNN C-LSTM achieved state-of-the-art single-site performance (NYU F1 0.78, UM F1 0.70), surpassing prior methods by 8-10%, but performance degraded substantially on the pooled multi-site ABIDE-I evaluation (F1 0.53), attributed to scanner/acquisition heterogeneity
narrative_row.key_limitations: No leave-site-out evaluation despite multi-site heterogeneity being identified as the cause of degraded performance; no motion/QC rule or diagnostic-instrument description reported; no code or data-availability statement
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Illustrates that an end-to-end raw-4D-volume classifier that performs well at single sites degrades sharply under multi-site heterogeneity when evaluated with ordinary (non-site-stratified) cross-validation.

kg_link.cohort_description: Single-site cohorts (NYU, UM) and a 19-site multi-site cohort from ABIDE-I; no stated QC/exclusion rule beyond site selection for balanced ASD/TD counts
kg_link.sites: NYU (184 subjects), UM (110 subjects) individually; 19 sites pooled (1100 subjects) for the multi-site experiment
kg_link.pipeline: C-PAC (Configurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes), 4mm MNI downsampling
kg_link.finding: Hybrid 3DCNN C-LSTM achieved F1 0.78 (NYU) and 0.70 (UM) for single-site ASD classification, but F1 dropped to 0.53 on the pooled 19-site ABIDE-I multi-site evaluation
evidence_quotes: For single sites experiments, we use the NYU and UM sites from ABIDE-I. Those provide the highest number of balanced (ASD/typically developing (TD)) subjects with 184 and 110 subjects respectively.
For the multi-site experiment we used ABIDE-I with 19 sites and 1100 subjects.

The results show that the proposed architecture 3DCNN C-LSTM outperforms other models on single site experiments by achieving mean test accuracies and F1 scores of 0.77 and 0.78 respectively for the NYU site and 0.71 and 0.7 on the UM site.
